description: {{ENGAGEMENT_SLUG}} - engagement-tier Claude plugin marketplace for the {{ENGAGEMENT_NAME}} engagement.

files.purpose: Cross-tool agent instructions. Source of truth for repo-wide agent behavior, ecosystem position, hosting options, compliance scope, branch and merge policy.
Claude Code-specific instructions. Imports AGENTS.md; adds naming convention, plugin conventions, stack and validation tables.
This file. Machine-readable manifest of root artifacts.
Repo overview: install instructions, three-tier model, three-surface compatibility, compliance note. In the template it also describes the template itself.
How an instance is created from the engagement template, initialized, protected, and kept current with template updates.
Reference copy of code ownership. Every plugin directory needs its own line (CI check: scripts/check-plugin-owners.py); a wildcard does not count.
Claude marketplace registry. Lists all plugins in this marketplace.

Naming config read by scripts/check-naming.py (CI, pre-commit, mise run validate): the engagement prefix for engagement-authored plugins and skills, and the generic plugins that carry no prefix. Schema: schemas/engagement.json.
One directory per plugin. Ships with the generic, unprefixed sdlc plugin (delivery-lifecycle skills); engagement plugins are named <prefix>-<slug> with the prefix from .engagement.json.
Project and document templates consumed by skills.
Rollout playbook and client-org setup guidance for running an engagement on this marketplace.
Plugin and skill authoring conventions: SKILL-AUTHORING.md, SKILL-TESTING.md, STUB-FORMAT.md.
How the marketplace is divided into plugins (generic, shared, engineering, department), who owns each, where an instruction lives, and how to add a plugin.
JSON Schema definitions for plugin.json, marketplace-entry.json and engagement.json (the root .engagement.json). Used by CI validation and mise run validate.

Repo tooling: init-engagement.sh (one-time placeholder fill-in for a new instance), template-state.sh (CI helper that detects an uninitialized template), check-naming.py (the plugin and skill naming rule), check-plugin-owners.py (every plugin has its own CODEOWNERS line and a complete OWNERS.md) and new-plugin.py (scaffolds a new engagement plugin with its owner records). The two checks run in CI and in mise run validate.
Claude Code-specific docs: VALIDATION.md (CI gate descriptions, hook limits), naming-convention.md (imported into CLAUDE.md).
Path-scoped authoring rules, one file per plugin, each with a paths: list so it loads only for that plugin's files.

Claude Code hooks wired in .claude/settings.json: PreToolUse client-name guard; PostToolUse format, yamllint, skill suffix check, stub format check and template index regen. Hook input is JSON on stdin. A local guard only; CI is the enforcement point.

CI workflows (validate, validate-frontmatter, scan-plugins, pr-automation, request-claude-review), git hooks, PR template, labeler, security-scan policy, and branch-protection.json (reference copy; applying it is a human act).

Engagement-specific sensitive names (client system names, partner IDs, personal identifiers) that must never appear outside plugins/*/references/ directories. One name per line. The CI isolation check enforces it; the Claude Code PreToolUse hook .claude/hooks/block-client-names.sh also refuses a Claude Code write locally. Do not list the engagement name itself.
Optional. GSD planning artifacts (PROJECT.md, roadmap, state) created when an instance runs GSD workflows. Committed to git when present.
